newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ABS says upward revisions in next Australian GDP.
newsitem.headline: ABS says upward revisions in next Australian GDP.

text.p: The June quarter 1997 report on Australian gross domestic product (GDP) will include upward revisions to the production based GDP measure, the Australian Bureau of Statitics (ABS) said on Wednesday.

The major improvements in estimating methods would affect the constant price gross product for the finance and insurance sector and the imputed bank service charge (ISBC), which to some extent will be offsetting. "Nevertheless, the changes are expected to lead to a significant upward revision to the level of GDP(P) in recent periods, although the impact on quarterly growth should be quite modest," the ABS said.

There will also be some smaller revisions to GDP(E) and GDP(I) as the method changes for estimating GDP(P) will affect corresponding components of private fianl consumption expenditure and exports of goods and services.
The ABS said comparisons between the existing and revised series will be included in the June quarter release.
The changes will incorporate changes in labour productivity, which has been assummed as a constant under the current system.
Current deflators for constant price estimates of private final consumption and exports of financial and and insurance services will be replaced by implicit price deflators.
The ABS said this would result in changes to the constant price estimates of GDP(E) and, as a consequence, to GDP(I).
